rationale: The Court unanimously rejects the Second Circuit’s “right to control” theory as an impermissible expansion of “money or property” under § 1343, distinguishing Carpenter as involving appropriation of a recognized proprietary asset. The likely majority opinion is a narrow, administrable holding (anchored in McNally/Cleveland/Kelly) preserving fraud prosecutions where the scheme’s object is obtaining traditional money or property, including true proprietary information.
